syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

chapters.title: Population: Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition

topics.title: Sources and distribution of population
topics.ncert_sections: Sources of Population Data; Distribution of Population

concepts.learning_objective: Recall how and since when population data are collected in India through the Census.
Describe the uneven spatial distribution of India's population among states.
Explain the physical, socio-economic and historical factors that shape population distribution.
State the meaning and spatial variation of population density in India.
Calculate and interpret physiological and agricultural densities.

topics.title: Growth of population and its measurement
topics.ncert_sections: Growth of Population; Population Doubling Time; Table 1.1

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between natural and induced components of population growth.
Calculate and interpret decadal growth rates of population.
Define population doubling time.
Identify the four phases of India's population growth and their causes.
Analyse the role of birth and death rates in the population explosion of 1951-1981.

topics.title: Regional variation in growth and the adolescent population
topics.ncert_sections: Regional Variation in Population Growth; adolescents; NYP-2014

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the population growth rates of different groups of states.
Explain the potential and vulnerabilities of India's adolescent and youth population and related policies.
Describe the distribution of rural population and the variation in village size.
Explain the growth and regional pattern of urban population in India.

topics.title: Linguistic and religious composition
topics.ncert_sections: Linguistic Composition; Linguistic Classification; Religious Composition

concepts.learning_objective: Describe India's linguistic diversity and the classification of languages into families.
Describe the spatial distribution of religious communities in India.

topics.title: Composition of working population
topics.ncert_sections: Composition of Working Population; Occupational Categories

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish between main workers, marginal workers and non-workers as defined by the Census.
Explain the spatial variation in work participation rate.
Interpret India's occupational structure and the sectoral shift of workers.

topics.title: Meaning of human settlements and rural-urban differences

concepts.learning_objective: Define a human settlement and explain how settling involves grouping people and apportioning territory.
Distinguish rural and urban settlements by economic base, functional links and social relations.
Identify the physical, cultural-ethnic and security factors that shape rural settlement types in India.
Describe clustered and semi-clustered settlements and the regions where they occur.
Describe hamleted and dispersed settlements, their causes and their regions.

topics.title: Urban settlements and evolution of towns in India

concepts.learning_objective: State the Census of India 1991 criteria for classifying a place as urban.
Classify Indian towns as ancient, medieval or modern and give examples of each.
Explain how the level of urbanisation is measured and state India's level in 2011.
Interpret the trends of urbanisation in India from 1901 to 2011 using Table 2.1.
Classify Indian towns by their dominant function with suitable examples.
Explain why growing cities become multifunctional and resist a single functional class.
State the objective and key features of the Smart Cities Mission.
Distinguish reporting area recorded by land revenue records from geographical area measured by the Survey of India.
Identify the nine land-use categories maintained in the land revenue records.
Classify uncultivated land as current fallow, fallow other than current fallow or culturable wasteland by duration.
Explain how growth and changing composition of the economy affect land-use.
Interpret the increases and declines in land-use categories between 1950-51 and 2019-20.
Define common property resources and distinguish them from private land.
Explain the importance of CPRs for landless and marginal farmers and rural women.

topics.title: Agricultural Land Use and Cropping Intensity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why land is more crucial to livelihoods dependent on agriculture than to other sectors.
Compute and interpret the total stock of cultivable land using Table 3.1.
Calculate cropping intensity and explain why a high cropping intensity suits India.

topics.title: Cropping Seasons and Types of Farming
topics.ncert_sections: Cropping Seasons in India; Types of Farming

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the kharif, rabi and zaid seasons and why they are not distinct in southern India.
Distinguish protective irrigation from productive irrigation.
Differentiate dryland farming from wetland farming by rainfall and crops.
Describe the distribution, conditions and yield patterns of rice, wheat and coarse cereals.
Explain the characteristics and distribution of pulses such as gram and tur.

topics.title: Oilseeds, Fibre Crops and Other Crops

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the main oilseed crops, their growing regions and leading states.
Describe the conditions and distribution of cotton and jute.
Explain the growing conditions and distribution of sugarcane, tea and coffee.

topics.title: Agricultural Development and Problems
topics.ncert_sections: Agricultural Development in India; Problems of Indian Agriculture

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Green Revolution strategy and later agricultural planning in India.
Analyse problems such as erratic monsoon, low productivity, indebtedness and underemployment.
Explain how faulty irrigation and farming practices degrade cultivable land.

topics.title: Water resources of India and surface water
topics.ncert_sections: Water Resources of India; Surface Water Resources

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and calculate India's total, available and utilisable water resources.
Explain the uneven spatial distribution and limited utilisation of surface water across river basins.
Compare the levels of groundwater utilisation among Indian states.
Describe the coastal lagoons and backwaters as a surface water resource and their uses.

topics.title: Water demand, utilisation and irrigation
topics.ncert_sections: Water Demand and Utilisation; Demand of Water for Irrigation; PMKSY

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the shares of agriculture, industry and domestic sectors in surface and groundwater use.
Explain why irrigation is needed in India and analyse the effects of its intensive use on groundwater.
State the vision and objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana.

topics.title: Emerging water problems and prevention of water pollution
topics.ncert_sections: Emerging Water Problems; Deterioration of Water Quality; Prevention of Water Pollution

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what water quality means and how pollutants deteriorate it.
Identify severely polluted rivers and evaluate legal and public measures to control water pollution.

topics.title: Water conservation, recycling and watershed management
topics.ncert_sections: Water Conservation and Management; Recycle and Reuse of Water; Watershed Management

concepts.learning_objective: Give examples of how water of lesser quality can be recycled and reused.
Explain the meaning and aims of watershed management.
Analyse community-based watershed programmes such as Haryali, Neeru-Meeru and Ralegan Siddhi.

topics.title: Rainwater harvesting and national water initiatives
topics.ncert_sections: Rainwater Harvesting; National Water Policy 2012; Jal Kranti Abhiyan

concepts.learning_objective: Describe methods and benefits of rainwater harvesting.
Interpret the salient features of India's National Water Policy, 2012.
State the aims and proposed activities of the Jal Kranti Abhiyan.
Classify minerals into metallic (ferrous, non-ferrous) and non-metallic (organic, inorganic) groups with examples.
Explain the uneven distribution, inverse quality-quantity relationship and exhaustibility of minerals.

topics.title: Distribution of minerals and mineral belts of India

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the three broad mineral belts of India and the minerals found in each.
Relate the location of India's minerals to the geological structure of the peninsula.

topics.title: Ferrous minerals: iron ore and manganese

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the types and the distribution of iron ore and its important mines in India.
State the uses of manganese and the distribution of its main producing areas.
Describe the occurrence of bauxite and its leading producing areas.
State the uses of copper and locate its main deposits in India.
State the properties and uses of mica and its producing areas.

topics.title: Conventional energy: coal, petroleum and natural gas
topics.ncert_sections: Energy Resources; Coal; Petroleum; Natural Gas

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the geological ages, types and major fields of coal in India.
Explain the occurrence, oilfields and types of refineries of petroleum in India.
Describe the uses and the main reserves of natural gas in India.
Identify uranium and thorium and the areas where they occur in India.
Trace the growth of India's nuclear programme and locate its important power projects.

topics.title: Non-conventional energy sources
topics.ncert_sections: Non-Conventional Energy Sources; Solar; Wind; Tidal and Wave; Geothermal; Bio-energy

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how solar and wind energy are tapped and where India has potential for them.
Describe tidal, geothermal and bio-energy and their examples in India.
Explain why sustainable development calls for conserving mineral and energy resources.
Evaluate measures such as recycling scrap, substitutes and reduced exports for conserving minerals.

chapters.title: Planning and Sustainable Development in Indian Context

topics.title: Meaning and approaches to planning; NITI Aayog

concepts.learning_objective: Explain planning as a process of thinking, formulating a scheme and implementing actions to achieve a goal.
Distinguish sectoral planning from regional planning.
State when and why the NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission.

topics.title: Target area planning and Hill Area Development Programme
topics.ncert_sections: Target Area Planning; Hill Area Development Programme

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why target area and target group approaches were introduced, with examples.
Describe the coverage, criteria and aims of the Hill Area Development Programmes.
Describe the objectives and changing emphasis of the Drought Prone Area Programme.
Identify how and where drought-prone areas of India were demarcated.

topics.title: Case study: Integrated Tribal Development Project in Bharmaur
topics.ncert_sections: Case Study - Integrated Tribal Development Project in Bharmaur Region

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the location, physical setting and the Gaddi community of the Bharmaur region.
Evaluate the infrastructural, social and economic outcomes of the ITDP in Bharmaur.
Trace how the concept of development evolved after World War II.
State and apply the Brundtland Report's definition of sustainable development.

topics.title: Case study: Indira Gandhi Canal command area
topics.ncert_sections: Case Study - Indira Gandhi Canal (Nahar) Command Area

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the origin, stages and flow and lift systems of the Indira Gandhi Canal.
Analyse the positive and negative impacts of canal irrigation on the command area.

topics.title: Measures for promotion of sustainable development in the IGC command area
topics.ncert_sections: Measures for Promotion of Sustainable Development

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the measures proposed to restore ecological balance in the command area.
Explain how social and economic sustainability can be achieved in the command area.

topics.title: Road Transport and National Highways
topics.ncert_sections: Land Transport, Road Transport, National Highways, National Highways Development Projects

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the size, history and classification of India's road network and the share of traffic it carries.
Explain the role of National Highways and the National Highways Authority of India.
Identify the Golden Quadrilateral, North-South and East-West Corridors and Bharatmala Pariyojana and their purposes.

topics.title: State, District, Rural and Other Roads
topics.ncert_sections: State Highways, District Roads, Rural Roads, Other Roads

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish State Highways, District Roads and Rural Roads and explain regional variation in rural road density.
Explain the work of the Border Roads Organisation and the purpose of international highways.
Recall the beginning of Indian Railways and explain why the system is divided into zones.
Distinguish broad, metre and narrow gauges by track width and length.
Analyse the development and regional distribution of railways, including the Konkan Railway and metro rail.

topics.title: Water Transport
topics.ncert_sections: Water Transport, Inland Waterways, National Waterways, Oceanic Routes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the features of inland water transport and the reasons for its decline.
Identify India's National Waterways and the authority that develops them.
Evaluate the importance of oceanic routes for India's foreign trade.

topics.title: Air Transport and Oil and Gas Pipelines
topics.ncert_sections: Air Transportation, Oil and Gas Pipelines

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the development of air transport in India, including UDAN and Pawan Hans.
Describe the advantages of pipelines and India's major oil and gas pipeline networks.

topics.title: Communication Networks
topics.ncert_sections: Communication Networks, Personal Communication System, Mass Communication System, Satellite Communication

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the internet is the most effective personal communication system.
Trace the development of radio and television as mass communication in India.
Distinguish the INSAT and IRS satellite systems and their uses.

topics.title: Changing pattern of India's international trade

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the growth in the volume of India's foreign trade since 1950-51 and the reasons for it.
Interpret India's exports, imports and trade balance from Table 8.1.

topics.title: Changing pattern of the composition of India's exports

concepts.learning_objective: Analyse changes in the shares of commodity groups in India's exports.
Describe the trends in traditional and new agricultural exports and their causes.

topics.title: Changing patterns of the composition of India's imports

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how India's import basket changed from foodgrains to fertilisers, petroleum and other goods.
Explain why the import of petroleum products has risen in India.
Interpret the region-wise pattern of India's import trade.
Identify the routes of India's foreign trade and the measures adopted to raise India's share in world trade.

topics.title: Sea ports as gateways of international trade
topics.ncert_sections: Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how colonial rule and Partition shaped the development of Indian ports.
Distinguish between major and minor ports of India by number and control.
Explain the meaning of hinterland and why its boundary is hard to fix.

topics.title: Major ports and their hinterlands
topics.ncert_sections: Ports of the west and east coasts

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the location, functions and hinterlands of the ports on India's west coast.
Identify the location, functions and hinterlands of the ports on India's east coast.
Evaluate the advantages and limitations of air transport in international trade.
Recall the number of major airports and the expansion under the UDAN scheme.

chapters.title: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems

topics.title: Environmental Pollution and Water Pollution
topics.ncert_sections: Environmental Pollution; Water Pollution; Namami Gange Programme

concepts.learning_objective: Classify environmental pollution by the medium through which pollutants are transported and diffused.
Identify natural and human sources of water pollution in India and their effects on health.
Explain the objectives of the Namami Gange Programme for cleaning the Ganga.
Identify the main sources and pollutants responsible for air pollution.
Explain the effects of air pollution such as disease, urban smog and acid rain.
Identify the main sources of noise pollution and why traffic noise is the biggest nuisance.
Explain how noise is measured and why noise pollution is location specific.

topics.title: Urban Waste Disposal
topics.ncert_sections: Urban Waste Disposal; Case Study: Daurala

concepts.learning_objective: Describe what solid waste is and the two sources from which it is disposed of.
Explain the health hazards of uncollected urban waste and the idea of treating waste as a resource.
Analyse the Daurala case of industrial groundwater contamination and its restoration on the polluter pays principle.
Explain the push and pull factors behind rural-urban migration in India.
Analyse the economic and social effects of migration on migrants and their families.
Explain how Indian urban centres are socially and economically differentiated.
Describe living conditions and socio-economic problems of slum dwellers.

topics.title: Land Degradation
topics.ncert_sections: Land Degradation; A Case Study: Jhabua

concepts.learning_objective: Define land degradation and identify the processes that cause it.
Classify wastelands according to natural and human-induced processes.
Evaluate community participation in watershed management in Jhabua district.
